name: rea
description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
one_liner: Hooks an AI assistant up to reverse-engineering tools so it can open another company's app, without the source code, and explain exactly how a feature works down to the raw program instructions.
buyer: A product manager at a small software company who saw a competitor ship a clever feature and wants an engineering-backed explanation of how it works before greenlighting a copy.
business_use_cases: A SaaS product team studies exactly how a competitor's sync or pricing feature works and builds an equivalent, backed by documented evidence instead of guesswork.
An authorized penetration tester uses it to speed up binary and app analysis during a paid security engagement.
A freelance consultant sells 'feature teardown' reports: pay me and I'll tell you precisely how that app does the thing you want to copy.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid competitive-feature teardown reports with a buildable implementation plan attached.
Bundle it into a security-consultancy's toolkit for authorized binary/app analysis engagements, billed per engagement.

steal_this: This weekend, pick one specific feature from a well-known app, run it through REA to document exactly how it works, and pitch that writeup as a paid teardown to a founder trying to build something similar. Stay honest about IP law: documenting mechanics for inspiration is fine, cloning pixel-for-pixel invites legal trouble.
